metadata.title: Claude Doesn't Design a New Zoom Chat App — It Assembles Into Yours.
metadata.topic: BUILD ZOOM TEAM CHAT APP · ANTHROPIC SKILL
metadata.purpose: Answer one real question in the Plain register: does Claude design a brand-new Zoom chat app, or does it assemble a bounded set of pieces into the chat you already have? Lands the carry-out that build-zoom-team-chat-app hands Claude one instruction file, and Claude assembles exactly what that file lists (bots, cards, buttons, slash commands) into the existing Zoom Team Chat — it never designs a new chat client.

beats.narration_text: Someone assumes Claude freely designs a brand new Zoom chat app from imagination. It doesn't. It assembles one — following a fixed instruction file that spells out exactly what to build.

beats.act: 1 anatomy — a skill is a folder
beats.narration_text: This assembly starts from something called a skill — a folder Claude reads before it works. Inside is one file, written in plain language, that spells out exactly what build-zoom-team-chat-app covers: messaging integrations, chatbot experiences, rich cards, buttons, slash commands, and chat webhooks. Claude reads the file, then follows it.

beats.narration_text: The steps run in order: read the file, work through each step exactly as written, then return the result. Nothing runs out of sequence unless a step itself says so.

beats.act: 3 constraint — one chat lane, six pieces
beats.narration_text: It only switches on after something else has already decided you're building for chat. From there its coverage is one list: user-scoped messaging integrations, chatbot experiences, rich cards, buttons, slash commands, and chat webhooks. Nothing on that list becomes a new Zoom client — every piece plugs into the chat that's already there.

beats.narration_text: Build Zoom Team Chat App doesn't give Claude a blank page. It gives Claude one instruction file, and Claude assembles exactly what that file lists — bots, cards, buttons, slash commands — into the Zoom chat you already have.
